title: Testable Specifications of Single-Synaptic Conscious Communication Through Phasic Signalling; Allowing Conscious Ontogenetic Development Through Synaptic Density, and Conscious Processing Within Subconscious Priors of Tonic Stimulation
content: The communication of consciousness between neurons within a single synapse is an underspecified occurrence, chemical transmission is essential for neural propagation, and neural propagation is essential within many existing measurements of consciousness. The development and plasticity of consciousness throughout an animal's lifetime requires grounded chemical distinctions of executive and non-executive processing and transmission. This paper's hypotheses propose chemical-conscious correlates between neurons, considered alongside established cognitive and environmental interaction, to specify how consciousness and its continuum are chemically produced at global scales, and developed ontogenetically during continuous environmental rationalization and neural propagation. Single-synaptic phasic transmitter transients may have evolved to allow executive function and selective consolidation within reflexive processing. These transmitter releases may be the chemical events through which subconscious stimulation allows phenomenal expression between neurons. This framing is consistent with phasic dynamics and tonic modulation of baseline synaptic stimulation, with each transmitter being differentiated by function. Phasic transients are further suggested to direct cortical spreading under tonic, epigenetic, and synaptic allowance. Because phasic releases fundamentally affect synaptic plasticity, while synapses determine the threshold and magnitude of phasic responses, this framing allows a developmental and individually variable model of consciousness. This development has potential to ground GWT/GNWT, IIT, Predictive Processing, and Affective Neuroscience, extending each framework by approaching phasic response as a mechanism of conscious variation and transmission at the scale of individual synapses. Because each hypothesis is specific and falsifiable, provided predictions and experimental directions can assist to determine the accuracy of each claim; given hypotheses are precise enough to fail and many of their correlating experiments are practical enough to proceed. If this account holds, it points toward practical improvements in depression treatments, therapeutics, memory rehabilitation, learning environment refinement strategies, and early developmental interventions.
